issues.legal_issue: Members of an unlawful assembly are not liable for murder when the evidence establishes that their common object extended only to causing grievous hurt, rather than committing murder.
material_facts: The appellants were members of an armed assembly that went to a disputed field to dispossess the opposing party by force.
The evidence showed that the assembly intended to cause such injury as was necessary to achieve that object.
Apart from the shooter and the person who supplied him a cartridge, no member of the assembly took part in assaulting the deceased, and the other weapons were not used.
The court found that the evidence supported, at most, an intention among the other appellants to commit an offence under Section 325 IPC.
issues.conclusion: For the appellants other than the shooter and the person who supplied him a cartridge, the court altered the conviction from Section 302/149 IPC to Section 325/149 IPC.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 149 IPC, the absence of an overt act by a member does not by itself disprove liability; the question depends on the facts of the case and whether the offence was within the unlawful assembly’s common object. The court found the common object here supported liability for grievous hurt under Section 325/149, but not murder under Section 302/149. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_from_assembly_murder_conviction and defendants_joined_forceful_dispossession and other_members_did_not_assault_victim and other_weapons_were_not_used and evidence_supported_only_grievous_harm_object

predicates.appeal_from_assembly_murder_conviction: The case is an appeal from a murder conviction based on membership in an unlawful assembly.
predicates.defendants_joined_forceful_dispossession: The defendants joined an assembly that used or intended force to dispossess another party.
predicates.other_members_did_not_assault_victim: The evidence showed that members other than the principal assailant and any identified accomplice did not assault the victim.
predicates.other_weapons_were_not_used: The evidence showed that weapons carried by the other assembly members were not used.
predicates.evidence_supported_only_grievous_harm_ob: The evidence supported an assembly object of causing grievous hurt, but not an object of committing murder.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns murder liability based on assembly membership, the other members did not assault the victim, their weapons were unused, and the evidence supports only an object of causing grievous hurt, the murder conviction is reduced to a grievous-hurt conviction based on assembly membership.

issues.legal_issue: Supplying ammunition to a shooter for the purpose of shooting the victim supports a finding of common intention to commit murder.
material_facts: Eyewitnesses testified that one appellant supplied a cartridge to the shooter so that he could shoot the deceased.
The shooter fired the gun and killed the deceased.
issues.conclusion: The court convicted that appellant under Section 302/34 IPC and upheld his life-imprisonment sentence.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 302 and 34 IPC apply where the evidence supports that the accused shared a common intention to commit murder; supplying a cartridge to the shooter for that purpose supported that finding here. No earlier cases are cited.

predicates.appeal_from_joint_murder_conviction: The case is an appeal from a murder conviction based on participation with another person.
predicates.defendant_supplied_ammunition_for_shooti: The defendant supplied ammunition to the shooter so the shooter could shoot the victim.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a joint murder conviction involves a defendant who supplied ammunition for the shooting, the joint murder conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A lengthy lapse after the offence, limited time already served, and the prospect of compensating the deceased’s family can justify reducing the remaining custodial sentence and imposing a compensatory fine.
material_facts: The appellants concerned had served only three to four months and had remained on bail.
About ten years had elapsed, and the court considered it not conducive to the interests of justice to return them to prison after that lapse.
The court considered compensation to the deceased’s family consistent with the socioeconomic purpose of modern sentencing policy.
issues.conclusion: For the appellants other than the appellant whose murder conviction and life sentence were upheld, the court reduced the custodial sentence to the period already served, imposed a fine of Rs. 5,000 on each with two years’ rigorous imprisonment in default, directed that the fine realised be paid to the deceased’s widow, and reduced the sentence under Section 147 IPC to the period already undergone.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the sentencing consideration that, in the circumstances of this case, compensation to the deceased’s family could serve the socioeconomic purpose of modern sentencing policy and avoid returning appellants to prison after a lengthy lapse. It relied on Sections 325/149 and 147 IPC for the convictions whose sentences it reduced. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_sentence and appellants_served_only_a_short_period and substantial_time_elapsed_since_offence and family_compensation_considered_appropriate

predicates.appeal_concerning_sentence: The case is an appeal in which the court is deciding the appropriate sentence.
predicates.appellants_served_only_a_short_period: The appellants had served only a short period in custody before the sentencing decision.
predicates.substantial_time_elapsed_since_offence: A substantial period had passed since the offence, during which the appellants had remained on bail.
predicates.family_compensation_considered_appropria: The court considered compensation to the deceased’s family an appropriate way to serve the purpose of sentencing.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns sentence, the appellants have served only a short period, substantial time has elapsed, and family compensation is considered appropriate, the custodial sentence is limited to time served and a compensatory fine is imposed.
